MaterialMaterialType.title:
- OPENVEX: https://github.com/openvex/spec
 - HELM_CHART: Static analysis output format
https://github.com/microsoft/sarif-tutorials/blob/main/docs/1-Introduction.md
 - EVIDENCE: Pieces of evidences represent generic, additional context that don't fit
into one of the well known material types. For example, a custom approval report (in json), ...
 - ATTESTATION: Chainloop attestation coming from a different workflow.
 - CSAF_VEX: https://docs.oasis-open.org/csaf/csaf/v2.0/cs03/csaf-v2.0-cs03.html
 - GITLAB_SECURITY_REPORT: Gitlab Application Security Reports https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/application_security/
 - TWISTCLI_SCAN_JSON: Twistcli scan output in json format: https://docs.prismacloud.io/en/compute-edition/30/admin-guide/tools/twistcli-scan-images
 - GHAS_CODE_SCAN: GitHub Advanced Security API reports
https://docs.github.com/en/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning?apiVersion=2022-11-28
 - GHAS_SECRET_SCAN: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/secret-scanning/secret-scanning?apiVersion=2022-11-28
 - GHAS_DEPENDENCY_SCAN: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependabot/alerts?apiVersion=2022-11-28
 - JACOCO_XML: Jacoco coverage reports https://www.jacoco.org/userdoc/importexport.html
 - SLSA_PROVENANCE: SLSA Provenance in the form of Sigstore Bundle
https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.0/provenance
https://docs.sigstore.dev/about/bundle/
 - CHAINLOOP_RUNNER_CONTEXT: The Chainloop CLI plugin for runner context
 - CHAINLOOP_PR_INFO: Pull Request / Merge Request metadata collected automatically during attestation
 - GITLEAKS_JSON: Gitleaks json report https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/README.md#reporting
 - CHAINLOOP_AI_AGENT_CONFIG: AI agent configuration collected automatically during attestation
 - CHAINLOOP_AI_CODING_SESSION: AI coding session telemetry collected during attestation
 - OPENAPI_SPEC: OpenAPI specification (v3.0, v3.1)
https://spec.openapis.org/oas/latest.html
 - ASYNCAPI_SPEC: AsyncAPI specification (v2.6, v3.0)
https://www.asyncapi.com/docs/reference/specification/latest
 - GRAPHQL_SPEC: GraphQL SDL schema
https://spec.graphql.org/
 - YELP_DETECT_SECRETS_BASELINE: detect-secrets baseline file https://github.com/Yelp/detect-secrets
 - SYSINTERNALS_SIGCHECK: Sysinternals sigcheck output in CSV format
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/sigcheck
 - SYSINTERNALS_ACCESSCHK: Sysinternals AccessChk text output https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/accesschk
 - CERTCC_DRANZER: CERT/CC dranzer ActiveX/COM control test report (plain text): a single
report or an archive (zip or tar.gz) holding the per-mode reports of one
run (-b, -p, -s, -t) https://github.com/CERTCC/dranzer
 - OSSF_SCORECARD_JSON: OpenSSF Scorecard result in JSON format
https://github.com/ossf/scorecard
 - RADAMSA_REPORT: radamsa -M metadata log, one record per generated iteration
https://gitlab.com/akihe/radamsa
 - RADAMSA_CRASHES: radamsa crashing inputs, a single file or a crashes/ archive (tar.gz or zip)
 - TRUFFLEHOG_JSON: TruffleHog secret scanning report in JSONL format (one JSON finding per line)
https://github.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog
 - COBERTURA_XML: Cobertura code coverage report in XML format
https://github.com/cobertura/cobertura
 - CHECKMARX_JSON: Checkmarx One native JSON report (ScanResultsCollection)
https://github.com/Checkmarx/ast-cli/blob/main/internal/wrappers/results-json.go
 - OVERSECURED_JSON: Oversecured mobile (Android/iOS) scan report, whole-scan JSON export
https://docs.oversecured.com/docs/guide-exporting-reports
 - PITEST_XML: PIT mutation testing report in its native XML format (mutations.xml)
https://pitest.org/
 - CHAINLOOP_AI_SECURITY_CONTEXT: Chainloop AI security context: vulnerability fingerprints mined from a
repository's fix history, the attack surfaces they share, ranked risks,
and byte-verifiable evidence anchors backing each claim

v1PolicyStatus.description:
Canonical, server-computed categorical policy outcome for an attestation.
Collapses the raw enforcement/bypass/violation signals on
AttestationItem.PolicyEvaluationStatus into a single flat value so that
list and describe surfaces can render a consistent badge without
re-deriving.

 - POLICY_STATUS_NOT_APPLICABLE: No policies were evaluated on this run
 - POLICY_STATUS_PASSED: Policies ran with no violations and no skips
 - POLICY_STATUS_SKIPPED: No violations but at least one evaluation was skipped
 - POLICY_STATUS_WARNING: Has violations but enforcement is advisory — run succeeded
 - POLICY_STATUS_BLOCKED: Has gated violations or enforced strategy with violations; not bypassed
 - POLICY_STATUS_BYPASSED: Enforcement would have blocked the run but was bypassed

v1PolicyStatusFilter.description: Server-side filter aligned 1:1 with PolicyStatus values.

total.title: Total number of policy evaluations that ran for this attestation

skipped.title: Number of evaluations that were skipped

violated.title: Total number of violations across all evaluations

has_gates.description:
Whether this run had gates in effect — any policy marked gate:true or
the contract using the ENFORCED blocking strategy. Independent of status:
a PASSED run can still have has_gates=true.

suppressed.description:
Number of suppressed violations across all evaluations. Excluded
from violated; kept in the CAS audit trail.

v1PolicyStatusSummary.description:
PolicyStatusSummary bundles the canonical PolicyStatus with per-evaluation
counters. It is surfaced on both WorkflowRunItem (list response) and
AttestationItem.PolicyEvaluationStatus (describe response) and is computed
by a single backend helper so list and describe cannot drift.

suppress.description:
Whether this violation was excluded from the policy gate (still kept
in the CAS audit trail).

v1PolicyViolationsFilter.description:
Deprecated: use PolicyStatusFilter which aligns 1:1 with PolicyStatus and
lets callers distinguish warning/blocked/bypassed from the coarse with/
without-violations split.

package_purl.title: Package URL of the affected component (e.g., pkg:golang/example.com/lib@v1.0.0)

description.title: Optional longer description of the vulnerability

v1PolicyVulnerabilityFinding.description:
Output schema for vulnerability findings from policy evaluation.
Used when a policy declares finding_type: VULNERABILITY.

user.title: The user who is a member of the project

group.title: The group who is a member of the project

role.title: The role of the user in the project

created_at.title: Timestamp when the project membership was created

updated_at.title: Timestamp when the project membership was last modified

latest_project_version_id.title: The ID of latest project version this member is associated with

parent_id.title: Optional parent resource ID for nested project memberships

v1ProjectMember.title: ProjectMember represents an user or group who is a member of a project

v1ProjectMemberRole.description:
- PROJECT_MEMBER_ROLE_UNSPECIFIED: Default role for a project member
 - PROJECT_MEMBER_ROLE_ADMIN: Admin role for a project member
 - PROJECT_MEMBER_ROLE_VIEWER: Viewer role for a project member
v1ProjectMemberRole.title: ProjectMemberRole defines the roles a member can have in a project

user_email.title: The user to add to the project

group_reference.title: The group to add to the project

v1ProjectMembershipReference.title: ProjectMembershipReference is used to reference a user or group in the context of project membership

v1ProjectServiceAddMemberResponse.title: ProjectServiceAddMemberResponse contains the result of adding a user to a project

members.title: The list of members in the project

v1ProjectServiceListMembersResponse.title: ProjectServiceListMembersResponse contains the list of members in a project

invitations.title: List of pending invitations for the project

v1ProjectServiceListPendingInvitationsRe.title: ProjectServiceListPendingInvitationsResponse contains a list of pending invitations for a project

projects.title: List of projects matching the request criteria

can_create_project.description:
Whether the caller may create a project in this organization. It is a
property of their organization role, not of any project, so it does not
belong on the items: an organization contributor, for instance, can be an
administrator of several projects and still create none. Clients offering
to create one need this to avoid an option that always fails.

v1ProjectServiceListResponse.title: ProjectServiceListResponse contains a paginated list of the organization's projects

v1ProjectServiceRemoveMemberResponse.title: ProjectServiceRemoveMemberResponse is returned upon successful removal of a user from a project

v1ProjectServiceUpdateMemberRoleResponse.title: ProjectServiceUpdateMemberRoleResponse is returned upon successful update of a member's role in a project

from.title: Index of the lower end of the connection, always smaller than to

to.title: Index of the higher end of the connection

v1ReferrerEdge.description: A connection between two referrers, as indexes into the request
v1ReferrerEdge.title: ReferrerEdge

digest.title: Digest of the referrer, i.e sha256:deadbeef or sha1:beefdead

kind.description: Kind of referrer, i.e CONTAINER_IMAGE, GIT_HEAD, ...

downloadable.title: Downloadable indicates whether the referrer is downloadable or not from CAS

references.title: References contains the list of related referrer items

created_at.title: CreatedAt is the timestamp when the referrer was created

metadata.title: Metadata contains additional descriptive information about the referrer

annotations.title: Annotations are key-value pairs associated with the referrer

v1ReferrerItem.description: It represents a referrer object in the system
v1ReferrerItem.title: ReferrerItem

digest.title: Digest of the referrer, i.e sha256:deadbeef or sha1:beefdead

kind.description: Kind of referrer, i.e CONTAINER_IMAGE, GIT_HEAD_COMMIT, ...

v1ReferrerRef.description: A reference to a referrer by digest and kind
v1ReferrerRef.title: ReferrerRef

nodes.description:
The referrers to find connections between. A digest alone does not identify a referrer, so
the kind travels with it.

This is a set. A referrer may be listed more than once — a client that collected referrers
from several attestations will have repeats — and is then reported at the position it first
appeared in. At least two distinct referrers are required.

project_name.title: Restricts the answer to a project, the same way DiscoverPrivate does

project_version.title: Only meaningful alongside project_name: version names are unique within a project

v1ReferrerServiceDiscoverEdgesRequest.description: Request to discover the edges between a set of referrers
v1ReferrerServiceDiscoverEdgesRequest.title: ReferrerServiceDiscoverEdgesRequest

edges.title:
Each connection once, regardless of the direction it is stored in, and referred to by the
first position its referrers were listed under in the request

result.title: Result is the discovered referrer item

pagination.title: Pagination information for the references list

name.title: unique, DNS-like name for the registration

description.title: Description of the registration, used for display purposes

workflow_file_path.title: Workflow file path that was used during build

authenticated.title: Whether the runner is authenticated, i.e. via the OIDC token

v1RunnerEnvironment.title: The runner environment in which the attestation was crafted

type.title: Type is the type of the scoped entity i.e project or org

id.title: ID is the id of the scoped entity

name.title: Name is the name of the scoped entity

v1WorkflowActivityWindow.description: WorkflowActivityWindow represents the time window for the last known workflow activity.

description.title: deprecated: description now belongs to the version, as it's versioned since the introduction of new contracts v2

scoped_entity.title: wether the contract is scoped to an entity in the organization

status.title: Detailed outcome of the apply operation

current_revision.description:
Current revision of the contract after the apply.
For a newly created contract this is the first revision; for an
unchanged contract it stays at the existing revision; for dry runs it
reflects the existing revision (0 when the contract does not exist yet).

contract_revision_latest.title: Current, latest revision of the contract

public.description:
Deprecated: public workflows were removed. This field is always false and
is retained only for wire compatibility; it will be removed in a future release.

workflow_template_id.description:
Optional reference to the platform workflow template this workflow was created from.
Empty when the workflow is not bound to any template.

project_version.title: kept for backwards compatibility with remote state storage

workflow_run_id.title: Not required since we might be doing a dry-run

state.title:
TODO: use runStatus enum below
deprecated field, use status instead

contract_revision_used.title: The revision of the contract used for this run

contract_revision_latest.title: The latest revision available for this contract at the time of the run

version.title: The version of the project the attestation was initiated with

has_policy_violations.description:
Whether the run has policy violations (null if no policies were evaluated)
Deprecated: use policy_summary.violated > 0, or the richer
policy_summary.status, which also distinguishes skipped / warning /
blocked / bypassed outcomes.

policy_summary.description:
Canonical policy status summary for this run (null if no policies were
evaluated). Carries both the categorical PolicyStatus and per-evaluation
counters so list consumers can render a badge without calling View.

verification.title: It will be nil if the verification is not possible (old or non-keyless attestations)

value.title: This value can be set in the contract or provided during the attestation
